top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman, B048) recognises a clearly identified discovery: selection of heterogeneous firms into exporting and reallocation across firms as a distinct channel for the gains from trade. The qualitative predictions (exporter premia, selection, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been tested in firm-level data across many countries for over twenty years, so maturity is established. Credit divides cleanly between the originating model (Melitz 2003) and its main extension (Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus FDI). The citation should be limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism and the gains-from-trade framework, so that it does not claim priority over the parallel empirical work of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum. I rank it above no award because it is the only awarding proposal on the slate and it meets the criteria of achievement, maturity and attribution. The remaining weaknesses, priority and dependence of welfare magnitudes on functional form, are real but are handled by tight wording. I moved to this view from B001 after weighing identification, the exclusion of Vishny, and the narrower claim a B001 citation could honestly make. Support counts played no part.
recusal_note: No connection to Melitz or Helpman is apparent from my profile. My corporate-finance field and Chicago Booth adjunct post are closer to B001, my earlier first choice, which is not on the slate. I have long committee overlap with Hassler, Krusell, Ellingsen and Svensson, and I am Vice President of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. These are disclosed, not adjudicated.
